body.statement:
Conditional on \((M,\Omega)\), fixed \(q\), uniform conditional sub-Gaussian moments, row-law factorization, conditional within-row block dependence, variance nondegeneracy, and the derived score-diffuseness bounds imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P(L/s\le z\mid M,\Omega)-\Phi(z)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and condition on \((M,\Omega)\).  Since \(\Omega\) is deterministic by \(\mathrm{ass:deterministic\mbox{-}mask}\), conditioning on \((M,\Omega)\) does not alter any of the conditional independence or moment assertions given \(M\).  For \((j,u)\in I\times J\), define
\[
 X_{ju}=s^{-1}w_{ju}\epsilon_{ju}.
\]
The weights and \(s\) are fixed under this conditioning by \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}variance}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:centered\mbox{-}noise}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[X_{ju}\mid M,\Omega]
 =s^{-1}w_{ju}\mathbb E_P[\epsilon_{ju}\mid M]=0.
\]

We next verify finite-range dependence rather than assume a central limit theorem.  Equip \(I\times J\subset\mathbb Z_+^2\) with the maximum metric.  Consider two collections of indices whose mutual distance is greater than \(q\).  Coordinates belonging to distinct rows generate conditionally independent sigma-fields by \(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}rows}\).  Within any common row, the corresponding time sets are separated by more than \(q\), so their sigma-fields are conditionally independent by \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}dependence}\).  Factoring over rows shows that the two full collections are conditionally independent.  Thus \(\{X_{ju}:(j,u)\in I\times J\}\) is a conditionally \(q\)-dependent random field.  If \(q=0\), it is also conditionally one-dependent, so below one may take \(k_0=\max\{q,1\}\).

Conditional row independence makes cross-row covariances vanish.  Within a row, conditional block dependence and conditional centering make covariances vanish at lags \(|h|>q\), while \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}stationary\mbox{-}covariance}\) gives covariance \(\gamma(h)\) at lag \(h\).  With the convention \(w_{j,u}=0\) outside \(J\), \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}variance}\) therefore yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{u=1}^T X_{ju}\middle|M,\Omega\right)
 &=\frac{1}{s^2}\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{h=-q}^{q}\gamma(h)
     \sum_{u=1}^T w_{ju}w_{j,u+h}\\
 &=\frac{s^2}{s^2}=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Division by \(s\) is valid because \(s^2\ge c_s/(nH)>0\) by \(\mathrm{ass:variance\mbox{-}nondegeneracy}\).

The conditional exponential-moment condition supplies the moment premise of the cited normal-approximation lemma.  Indeed, for an absolute numerical constant \(C_3<\infty\), the elementary bound
\[
 |x|^3\le C_3K^3\exp(x^2/K^2),\qquad x\in\mathbb R,
\]
and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}subgaussian\mbox{-}noise}\) imply, almost surely,
\[
 \sup_{j,u}\mathbb E_P[|\epsilon_{ju}|^3\mid M,\Omega]
 \le 2C_3K^3.
\]
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:chen\mbox{-}shao\mbox{-}finite\mbox{-}range\mbox{-}normal\mbox{-}bound}\) conditionally, with \(p_0=3\), \(d_0=2\), \(k_0=\max\{q,1\}\), and index set \(I\times J\).  Since \(\sum_{j,u}X_{ju}=L/s\), the preceding centering, dependence, moment, and unit-variance calculations verify all of its premises.  Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P\!\left(\frac{L}{s}\le z\middle|M,\Omega\right)-\Phi(z)\right|\\
 &\quad\le
 75(10k_0+1)^4\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{u=1}^T
 \mathbb E_P[|X_{ju}|^3\mid M,\Omega]\\
 &\quad\le C_qK^3s^{-3}\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{u=1}^T|w_{ju}|^3\\
 &\quad\le C_qK^3
 \left(s^{-1}\max_{j,u}|w_{ju}|\right)
 \left(s^{-2}\sum_{j,u}w_{ju}^2\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
By the already established \(\mathrm{lem:score\mbox{-}diffuseness}\), the first factor in the last line is \(o(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), and the second is \(O(1)\) uniformly over that class.  The constants \(q\) and \(K\) are fixed by \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\mbox{-}known\mbox{-}range}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}subgaussian\mbox{-}noise}\).  Taking the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) in the displayed bound proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P\!\left(\frac{L}{s}\le z\middle|M,\Omega\right)-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
which is the claimed uniform conditional central limit theorem.
body.justification: A uniform finite-range random-field Berry--Esseen argument derives the Gaussian limit from primitive conditional dependence, moments, and diffuse weights.
body.gap: Existing serial factor central limit theorems do not cover this complete three-block influence array under deterministic causal-block masking.
body.consumer: The Wald theorem uses this derived score limit instead of assuming asymptotic normality.
